temperatures in the mid 60s to low 70s, with widespread Moderate

Carquinez Strait, and foothills.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Mobile Coastal County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 8 AM
CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Around 2 feet MHHW, water begins to cover
portions of Shell Belt and Coden Belt Roads. Roads may have some
debris washed up on them.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Nuckolls, NE; Thayer, NE
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 10:49AM CDT until October 2 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the Little Blue River in East Central Nuckolls County
in south central Nebraska and Central Thayer County in south
central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1031 AM CDT, As of 945 AM CDT Friday, the gauge along the
Little Blue River north of Deshler was at 16.5 feet, which was
just above minor flood stage of 16.0 feet. Meanwhile, at 1015 AM
CDT the gauge at Hebron reported a stage of 13.5 feet, which was
right at minor flood stage. As a result, minor, lowland flooding
continues along the immediate reach of the Little Blue River from
east-central Nuckolls County downstream across all of Thayer
County. Based on trends over the last 12 hours, the river is
expected to continue a very slow, gradual fall through the rest
of today, and the gauges near Deshler and Hebron could slip
slightly below flood stage by sometime Friday evening. However,
there is some uncertainty regarding how quickly water levels will
drop, and it is possible that areas along the river especially
east of Hebron to the Jefferson County line could continue to
experience minor flooding through at least early Saturday.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Little Blue River.
- Locations immediately along the Little Blue River across Thayer
and far eastern Nuckolls counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 6:50AM AKDT until October 3 at 7:45AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
The Mendenhall Lake crested early Friday morning, and the Mendenhall
River will crest shortly. Flooding is ongoing, and is expected to
continue near Mendenhall Lake and River before coming to an end later
this morning as water levels decrease rapidly behind the crest.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent or occurring. Water levels will
decrease now that the Mendenhall Lake has crested, and Mendenhall
River will crest through the next hour.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 648 AM AKDT, gauge data reports that the Mendenhall Lake has
crested, with the Mendenhall River to follow suit in the next
hour. Flooding continues near The Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 5:45am the stage was 10.18 feet, which was the crest.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 10.18 feet occurred at 5:45am Friday
morning. Water levels exceeded moderate flood stage of 10 feet
around 5:00am Friday. Water levels will fall below minor flood
stage late morning Friday.

Impacts:
At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.
At 9.0 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.
At 9.5 feet: Water levels up to 0.5 feet will cover Skaters Cabin
Road between Skaters Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead. Campsite 7
will be flooded with water starting to flow over the road between
campsites 8 and 9 in the Mendenhall Campground.
At 10.0 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with
up to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

The cold water temperatures can increase the threat of hypothermia
and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River at Birdsprings.

* WHEN...Until 215 AM MST /315 AM MDT/ Saturday.

occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

River at Winslow have crested but remain above action stage.

Birdsprings area through tonight.

At 7:00am MST /8:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.33 feet.

Navajo Route 71 near Birdsprings will flood, and Leupp will be

Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests at
Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southeast Texas, including
the following areas, in south central Texas, Coastal Jackson and
Inland Jackson. In southeast Texas, Austin, Brazos, Burleson,
Coastal Harris, Colorado, Fort Bend, Grimes, Inland Harris,
Montgomery, Walker, Waller, Washington and Wharton.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Over the last 24 hours, much the watch area has seen between 3-6
inches with a swath of 6-8+ inches observed from southwestern
Montgomery County down through western Harris County. Showers and
thunderstorms capable of producing heavy downpours will continue
to impact the watch area through this evening. Embedded training
rain rates of 2-4 inches per hour will be possible with the deep
tropical airmass overhead. Locations that experience training
storms with heavier rainfall rates may  experience rapid runoff
that could result in flash flooding. Those living in areas prone
to flooding should be prepared to take action should flooding
develop. Stay weather aware and be ready to take action when
Flash Flood Warnings are issued, particularly wireless emergency
alert Flash Flood Warnings for considerable and/or catastrophic
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 2 at 10:36PM ChST until October 5 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
10 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...North and west facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM ChST Monday. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, through Monday evening. For the High Rip
Current Risk, through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may
be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.
If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against
the current. If able, swim in a direction following the
shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave
for help.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 2 at 9:21PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TYPHOON WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FOR AGRIHAN AND PAGAN IN THE
CNMI...

...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN NEARLY STATIONARY AS IT CONTINUES WEST-
NORTHWEST AWAY FROM ANATAHAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
A Typhoon Warning is now in effect for Agrihan and Pagan in the
CNMI.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Typhoon Warning is now in effect for Agrihan and Pagan in the
CNMI.

A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan, and
Alamagan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Warning means that typhoon conditions, including winds
of 74 mph or more are expected, with tropical storm force winds
beginning within 24 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions,
including winds of 39 to 73 mph, are expected within 24 hours.
A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions are possible within
24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 8 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was
located near latitude 17.1N, longitude 144.7E. This was about 80
miles northwest of Alamagan, 100 miles southwest of Pagan, 130
miles south-southwest of Agrihan, and 250 miles north of Guam.
Storm motion was west-northwest, 300 degrees, at 2 mph. Storm
intensity was 70 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-wan is very slowly pivoting to the north as it
moves away from Anatahan, and is expected to continue to intensify
through tonight and Saturday as it turns north-northeast toward
Agrihan and Pagan, likely becoming a typhoon later tonight. The
latest forecast shows Choi-wan as a Category 1 typhoon as it
passes just west of Pagan and moves near or over Agrihan, sometime
Saturday afternoon, and a Typhoon Warning has been issued for
Agrihan and Pagan. During this time, the wind field will continue
to expand slightly, exposing Tinian and Saipan to tropical storm
conditions a little longer, possibly into late Saturday night.
While showers have tapered a little earlier in the day, the
intense rainbands that pummeled Guam and Rota earlier this
morning are now being pulled toward Tinian and Saipan, with
additional heavy showers and thunderstorms expected tonight.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind
conditions associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the
advice of your local emergency managers and officials, and
continue to monitor forecasts by the National Weather Service
office in Tiyan, Guam. Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-
clear is given.

Preparations for Tropical Storm Choi-wan should be complete.
Remain in suitable shelter, such as a cave or sturdy concrete
structure. Shelter in place until the all-clear is given.

.WIND INFORMATION...
North to northeast winds of 25 to 35 mph will turn toward the
southeast and increase tonight as Choi-wan slowly pivots north-
northeast toward the northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially
becoming a typhoon later tonight to the west of Alamagan.
Tropical storm force winds of 39 to 50 mph look to continue
through Sunday. Winds are expected to increase to strong tropical
storm-force of 58 to 65 mph for Alamagan and Pagan late tonight,
then sometime Saturday morning for Agrihan. Typhoon force winds
greater than 74 mph are expected for Pagan and Agrihan during time
of closest passage on Saturday in the late morning to early
afternoon for Pagan, and Saturday afternoon to evening for
Agrihan. Typhoon conditions remain possible for Alamagan, but are
not expected at this time.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf of 8 to 12 feet along east and south-facing reefs
are expected to continue, to then spread along north and west-
facing reefs as the center moves north-northeast parallel to the
northern CNMI tonight through Saturday night, increasing by
several feet during this time. As Choi-wan continues to
strengthen, surf will continue to increase, likely becoming
dangerous by early next week. Significant coastal erosion and some
coastal inundation is expected during Choi-wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered
thunderstorms are expected through tonight, which is expected to
produce rainfall totals of 8 to 14 inches by early Monday morning,
with up to 20 inches of rainfall possible near the center of the
system.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 1:56AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Scott County in east central Iowa...
Henry IL County in northwestern Illinois...
Mercer County in northwestern Illinois...
Rock Island County in northwestern Illinois...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 150 AM CDT, Rainfall has diminished throughout the warned
area. Total rainfall amounts of 2 to 5 inches have occurred
across the warned area resulting in flooding. Law Enforcement and
Emergency Management report several roads either partially
inundated, or totally inundated with standing water and some are
closed. Duck Creek is out of its banks leading to several road
closures in Davenport and Bettendorf.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 11:46PM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding along the West Fork Big Blue River in
portions of York and Fillmore counties continue.

* WHERE...Southeastern York County in east central Nebraska...
Northwestern Fillmore County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations continues.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1136 PM CDT, automated river gauges continue to indicate
ongoing minor flooding along the West Fork Big Blue River, as a
result of heavy rainfall over the last few days. As of 11:00PM
CDT, an automated gauge north of Grafton reported a stage of
13.3,  which was 2.3 feet above the minor flood stage of 11.0
feet. Given the recent trends indicating a substantial slowdown
of increasing water levels, we suspect that the water levels may
be soon to crest tonight. It is likely that water levels along
the West Fork Big Blue River will remain in minor flood stage
until at least sometime Friday or Friday night before dropping
back below flood stage.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Fork Big Blue River, Turkey Creek, Little Sandy Creek,
Beaver Creek, Big Sandy Creek, Pawnee Creek, School Creek, Sleepy
Hollow Creek, Scott Creek, Buffalo Creek, Johnson Creek, Walnut
Creek, South Fork Turkey Creek, Galaway Creek, Stone Creek, Dry
Sandy Creek, Dove Creek, Little Blue River, Thirtytwo Mile Creek,
Dry Run Creek, Liberty Creek and Oak Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction, and rural areas along the West Fork Big Blue
River both upstream and downstream of McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 1 at 7:39PM PDT until October 2 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 0.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 0.9 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 3:58 PM
Friday 10/02. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
